title: ASML’s Next Growth Engine Takes Shape as Intel Tops 1 Million High NA Wafers
source_used: Tom's Hardware (original 7 Sep 2026 coverage); TipRanks blocked (403)
key_facts: Intel announced on Monday 7 Sep 2026 that it had processed more than one million 300-mm wafers on High-NA EUV scanners, less than two and a half years after its first tool was assembled.
Intel's count includes wafers processed during tool installation and certification, R&D and production.
Intel certified the High-NA tools for its 18A process earlier this year and uses them for some Panther Lake processors.
Intel has two ASML Twinscan EXE:5000 tools and at least one EXE:5200B scanner.
Tom's Hardware says ASML reported in April that all High-NA scanners shipped by then had processed over 500,000 wafers, so Intel has now processed more than the rest of the industry combined.
Intel is also working on larger 6x12-inch photomasks to avoid stitching two half-fields together, which cuts throughput from 175 to 125 wafers an hour on an EXE:5200B.
Moving to larger masks would need big changes across the mask supply chain, and ASML's roadmap still assumes 6x6-inch masks.
quote_evidence: Intel announced on Monday that it had processed more than one million 300-mm wafers using its High-NA EUV scanners, less than two and a half years after its first tool was assembled.
Intel's one million wafers figure includes wafers processed during tool installation and certification, R&D, and production.
why_it_matters_hint: Intel is using ASML's newest chip-printing machines at larger scale than anyone else, but the count includes test and research wafers.
